summary: The four figures show Moving Average Peak-to-Peak rail roughness traces against position (upper panels) and one-third-octave roughness spectra from 2000 mm down to 3.15 mm wavelength (lower panels) for Eastbound Bethnal Green to Mile End on the Central line, covering LHR (Figures 1–2, -4.6276 to 1534.0000 m) and RHR (Figures 3–4, 0.0000 to 1544.5434 m) in the 30–100 mm and 100–300 mm wavelength bands.

On the LHR, both bands have a 41% (0.626 km) exceedance above their respective thresholds, with a main average P-P of 16.5 µm (>10 µm) in the 30–100 mm band and 39.2 µm (>30 µm) in the 100–300 mm band; the longest continuous rough stretch runs from roughly 720 m to 1210 m (peaking at ~135 µm at ~869 m in 30–100 mm and ~288 µm at ~883 m in 100–300 mm), while the 100–300 mm trace also has a cluster of taller spikes between 165 m and 220 m reaching a global maximum of ~325 µm at ~169 m.
On the RHR, the main average P-P and exceedance are lower than on the LHR in both bands: 10.9 µm with 33% (0.504 km) >10 µm for 30–100 mm, and 35.7 µm with 34% (0.519 km) >30 µm for 100–300 mm.

The RHR position traces concentrate their highest roughness in three main stretches: roughly 85–280 m (where RHR 30–100 mm reaches its global maximum of ~112 µm at ~262 m and ~110 µm at ~166 m, and RHR 100–300 mm reaches ~318 µm at ~203 m), 725–910 m (where RHR 100–300 mm reaches its global maximum of ~378 µm at ~886 m), and 1285–1525 m (peaking at ~85 µm in 30–100 mm and ~195 µm in 100–300 mm).

For each rail, the 30–100 mm and 100–300 mm figures display the same full-range one-third-octave spectrum curve in the lower panel, falling overall from 43.5 dB (LHR) and 45.0 dB (RHR) at 2000 mm to -6.0 dB (LHR) and -8.5 dB (RHR) at 3.15 mm.

Comparing the two spectra, the LHR curve is higher than the RHR curve at every band from 125 mm down to 3.15 mm (by 2.5–3.5 dB across 125–31.5 mm and by 5–6.5 dB at 12.5 mm and 6.3–4.0 mm), whereas the RHR curve is 0.5–5.5 dB higher than the LHR curve across the longer wavelengths from 2000 mm to 160 mm, with a local peak of 24.5 dB at 200 mm.

summary: The four figures show rail roughness along ~1.54 km of the Eastbound Central line from Bethnal Green to Mile End for two rails (LHR on page 1, RHR on page 2) and two moving-average peak-to-peak wavelength bands (30-100mm and 100-300mm).

On the LHR, the 30-100mm trace (Figure 1) has a main average P-P of 16.5 µm with 41% (0.626 km) exceeding 10 µm and a global peak of ~135 µm at ~883 m, while the 100-300mm trace (Figure 2) has a main average P-P of 39.2 µm with 41% (0.626 km) exceeding 30 µm and peaks up to ~324 µm at ~168 m and ~284 µm at ~883 m.

On the RHR, the 30-100mm trace (Figure 3) has a lower main average P-P of 10.9 µm with 33% (0.504 km) exceeding 10 µm and peaks of ~110-111 µm at ~168 m and ~265 m, while the 100-300mm trace (Figure 4) has a main average P-P of 35.7 µm with 34% (0.519 km) exceeding 30 µm and a global peak of ~385 µm at ~884 m.

Both rails show sustained rough activity between roughly 725 m and 905 m (continuing above threshold to ~1200 m on LHR and in shorter stretches on RHR), plus a rough cluster around 100-285 m and, on RHR, an additional rough zone between ~1295 m and ~1510 m.

Within each rail, the lower spectrum panel is identical between the 30-100mm and 100-300mm figures (Figure 1 matches Figure 2; Figure 3 matches Figure 4), falling from ~44-45 dB rel 1 µmRMS at 2000 mm to below 0 dB at short wavelengths.

Comparing the two spectra, RHR is 1-5 dB higher than LHR at wavelengths from 2000 mm down to 200 mm (with a local peak of 24.4 dB at 200 mm), whereas LHR is higher than RHR across 160 mm to 3.15 mm (with local peaks of 23.0 dB at 125 mm, 3.8 dB at 25 mm, 1.3 dB at 12.5 mm and 1.4 dB at 5 mm).

Both rails show sustained rough activity between roughly 725 m and 905 m (continuing above threshold to ~1200 m on LHR and in shorter stretches on RHR), plus a rough cluster around 100-285 m and, on RHR, an additional rough zone between ~1295 m and ~1510 m.

Within each rail, the lower spectrum panel is identical between the 30-100mm and 100-300mm figures (Figure 1 matches Figure 2; Figure 3 matches Figure 4), falling from ~44-45 dB rel 1 µmRMS at 2000 mm to below 0 dB at short wavelengths.

Comparing the two spectra, RHR is 1-5 dB higher than LHR at wavelengths from 2000 mm down to 200 mm (with a local peak of 24.4 dB at 200 mm), whereas LHR is higher than RHR across 160 mm to 3.15 mm (with local peaks of 23.0 dB at 125 mm, 3.8 dB at 25 mm, 1.3 dB at 12.5 mm and 1.4 dB at 5 mm).
